title: Phase 7 telemetry run snapshot
description:
Schema for analysis/telemetry/run_<run_id>.json produced by scripts/phase_7_telemetry_collector.py (v1.2.4, P1+P2). One file per pipeline run; the file is an OBSERVATION of the canonical state at run time, not an assertion ABOUT it. Phase 7 L1 (the future telemetry miner; v1.2.x+ candidate) will read these snapshots across multiple runs to detect tunable-knob drift and propose tuning patches via tunables.yaml. Strictly read-only with respect to canonical state. NOT F5-validated (operator-side observation, not promotion gate). NOT in POLICY_GLOBS (no canon-hash interaction). Token-shape scrubbing inherits from privacy_scan (we never observe tokens — only structural KPIs / counts). See docs/phase_7_design.md for the full L0 → L1 → L2 architecture.

v1.2.4 ships only the SHAPE + collector — the miner that consumes these files is L1 / v1.2.5+ scope. Operators may capture telemetry runs today + retain them for the future miner without a backend.

schema_version.description: Telemetry-run shape version. v1.2.4 ships 1.0; bumped on breaking shape changes.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when this snapshot was captured. Same shape as marker.timestamp.

run_id.description: Operator-supplied run identifier (CLI flag --run-id=<id>, or auto-generated from timestamp). Lets a future L1 miner aggregate observations across N runs without confusing them. Lowercase alphanumeric + hyphen + underscore.

plugin_version.description: Plugin manifest version at capture time (e.g., '1.2.4'). Captures which plugin release produced the observation.

canon_policy_version.description: Canon policy version + hash at capture time. Lets the future L1 miner correlate observations to specific policy state (e.g., 'KPI-001 dipped on the same day canon hash moved from X to Y' — that's evidence the canon change caused the dip).

workspace_path.description: Optional. Repo-relative or absolute path to the workspace this snapshot reflects. Operator-controlled — may be elided for privacy.

kpi_observations.description: Per-KPI observation block. v1.2.4 ships KPI-001 (weighted ClaimStrength coverage) + KPI-006 (story-to-claim coverage ratio). Future KPIs add as additional keys; the current key set is documentary.

kpi_001_weighted_coverage.description: KPI-001 weighted: sum(ClaimStrength for direct claims with bound SourceID+ExcerptID) / count(direct claims). Target ≥ 0.75 per reliability_tier_spec.md.

kpi_006_story_coverage.description: KPI-006: |A70 stories with at least one direct A72 row| / |A70 stories|. Target ≥ 0.90 per bsa-traceability-matrix SKILL.md §KPI-006.

validator_observations.description: Optional. Per-validator outcome counts (pass/fail/warn). Empty {} when no validators ran in this snapshot's window. Future-extensible: add per-validator keys as new validators land.

threshold_trigger_counts.description: Optional. Counts of times each tunable-threshold triggered during the run window (e.g., 'EpistemicInsufficiency' fired 3 times). The future L1 miner uses these to detect threshold-tuning candidates: if a threshold fires 0 times across 30 runs, it's probably too loose; if it fires every run, too strict.

kpis_at_target.description: Number of KPIs whose `value` meets `target` (per the per-KPI comparison operator).

kpis_below_target.description: Number of KPIs whose `value` is below target. Operator-readable signal: 'X of Y KPIs missed target this run'.

value.description: Observed value (e.g., 0.82 for KPI-001 weighted coverage). null when the input artifact required to compute is absent (pre-Stage-1 runs etc.).

target.description: Target value at the time of capture (sourced from config/tunables.yaml or the canonical reference doc).

comparison.description: Comparison operator for value-vs-target. Most KPIs are >= (higher is better).

status.description: Pre-computed verdict. n/a when value is null. The operator-readable summary block aggregates these.

numerator.description: Optional. The raw numerator that produced `value`. Lets the L1 miner detect data shape (e.g., zero-numerator vs zero-denominator).

denominator.description: Optional. The raw denominator that produced `value`.
